messages.subject: "cluster sizes are 0" warning
parts:
Hello 

I'm having a problem trying to analyze data with clusters. I get a warning that "**One or more cluster sizes are 0. These observations will be used in cluster size estimation. If you intended to code these values as missing, please enter them as -1.0 **" 
This warning causes  
** Error: Cannot log transform a cluster size of zero  - choose a different option for size bias regression. **

I've checked my data multiple times and there are no 0 values in the cluster size. I have also tried with a small part of the data (attached) and I still have the same problem.

Do you have any idea why this may be happening? 

Thanks 
Sylvia

messages.author: 75e0b0abcbafbc7d
messages.subject: Re: {Suspected Spam} [distance-sampling] "cluster sizes are 0" warning
parts:
Sylvia

Thanks for your clarification that you are using Distance for Windows.  Studying your data, I see that you are analysing pellet count data for roe deer.  You have recorded the number of pellets in each pellet group you detected; is that correct?

When you created your Distance for Windows project, I suspect you ticked the box that said "clusters of objects"


For pellet surveys, this is not what you want to do.  Your analysis will consist of estimating the density of pellet groups in your study area, then you will estimate the number of pellet groups produced per deer per day as well as the rate at which pellet groups decay.  As you see, the focus is on the pellet group, not individual pellets.

You can still have number of pellets in your project, perhaps to use as a covariate that influences detectability along with distance from transect.  But because you ticked "clusters of objects", Distance for Windows is treating the number of pellets in a particular way that is causing difficulties.

Create a new project and tick "single objects", I think that will resolve your problems.  Let me know if you have other questions.
